summary: Intermittent missing rerank hits when embedding payloads are split across storage shards
summary_details: Customer reports intermittent loss of top-k results from reranker endpoint. Issue correlates with large batched embedding uploads which appear to be split across underlying storage shards; reranker receives a partial set of vectors for queries that reference a cut boundary and returns reduced recall and no obvious errors to the client.
description: Issue summary: Searchly Labs (dedicated customer) observes intermittent missing hits and lower-than-expected recall from the rerank endpoint when they upload large CSVs of documents that produce many embeddings. Impact: user-visible reduction in top-10 recall for certain queries (10-30% of queries during bulk upload windows); affects production search features for a subset of customers in us-east-1. Environment: Dedicated cluster for Searchly Labs in prod (us-east-1). Embeddings are generated with open-embed-2-small and stored in sharded object store via embeddings-service. Steps to reproduce: 1) Upload >100k documents via bulk ingestion API with batch_size=1024 and chunking enabled. 2) Wait for background embed generation and storage. 3) Query rerank endpoint for known query set (provided by customer) that historically returns N items; observe topk drop. 4) Re-run same query after re-running a reindex and sometimes results return to expected recall. Expected behavior: reranker should consistently return top-k candidates matching full index regardless of how embeddings are sharded. Actual behavior: reranker returns fewer candidates or missing top items for queries where candidate set spans shard boundary. No 5xx or client-visible errors; sometimes a silent reduction in results. Logs/trace: embedding-service logs show "write_completed" events for batches, storage-shard-router logs show occasional "partial_batch_routed" warnings at the same timestamps as rerank regressions. Reranker logs show shortened candidate vector counts for impacted queries (e.g. expected 512 vectors, observed 478). Attachments: customer-provided sample query payloads and CSV manifest (attached externally).
steps_to_reproduce: Customer bulk uploads >100k documents with batch_size=1024 and chunking enabled
Run the customer's validation query set against rerank endpoint and compare top-k results to baseline
If results show missing hits, trigger a manual reindex (temporary recovery observed)

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: shard boundary cut during streaming write caused some vectors to be left uncommitted in index metadata (meta index referenced only first half of batch)
Verified via storage audit: for several batch_ids we find mismatch between embedding objects and index pointers for shard transitions (objects present in s3 but index pointer not updated)
Reproduced locally by forcing upload chunk boundary alignment to chunk_size=8192 bytes; observed same missing-candidate symptom in staging
Ruled out model inference errors: embeddings were produced consistently; vector values present in object store but absent in vector index for a time window
Observed correlation with concurrent reindex job that updates shard manifest; race condition suspected where shard-manifest update may overwrite pointers for overlapping batch ranges

impact: Degraded search quality (missed top-k) for customers performing large bulk ingest; intermittent but repeatable when uploads align to shard boundaries. No increased latencies or 5xx observed; impacts trust and user experience.
mitigation_steps: Advised customer to stagger uploads into smaller batches (<=256) as a temporary workaround
Triggered a targeted reindex for Searchly Labs to restore missing index pointers
Applied temporary guard in storage-shard-router to ensure atomic manifest update when batch spans shards (hotfix rollback to stable after verification)
resolution_summary: Hotfix introduced to make manifest update idempotent and to delay pointer swap until all shard writes confirm. Hotfix validated in canary and then rolled out to prod for affected region. Manual reindex restored missing vectors for Searchly Labs. Root cause: race between chunked write completion and shard-manifest swap leading to index pointer divergence at shard boundaries. Long-term plan: add transactional manifest updates, implement post-write verification, and add automated detection dashboards for candidate_vector_count drops.
resolution_actions: Backfilled index pointers for affected batches for Searchly Labs (manual reindex)
Released embeddings-service v1.9.3 with idempotent manifest swap and post-write verification
Added alert in Grafana for reranker candidate_vector_count deviation >10% from expected
Create runbook for shard-boundary ingestion failures and add to confluence
rollback_plan: If the new manifest-swap logic causes regressions, we will revert to previous stable routing (embeddings-service v1.9.2) and perform coordinated reindex while investigating race conditions offline.
postmortem_tasks: Add unit/integration tests that simulate chunked boundaries and concurrent reindex
Create a migration tool to validate index-pointer consistency across shards
Notify customers in deduped incident communication and update docs with recommended batch sizing
